contexts.text: Cares little for the Old Testament.
The Lord takes much care of them, because they have lived a pious life...

A Spirit receives much more excellent capacities when separated from the body, (and thus from) cares for food, clothing, habitation, children, and many other things, about which they think nothing in the other life... AC 1941. AC 3660:3. AC 4214:3.
The Lord gives the Angels what to think every moment... thus are they devoid of cares and solicitudes...

These things appear of slight consequence to man, in whose care and heart are worldly and corporeal things... but the same are precious to the Angels, in whose care and heart are celestial and spiritual things. AC 3688:2. AC 4096:2. AC 5224:2. AC 6648.
He trusts in the Lord, and cares nothing about all other things...
He who acts from charity... cares nothing for the things of faith, or truth...
Under Anxiety, see this reference, and at AC 3938:7. AC 6202. AC 8247.

If they do not apprehend them in the life of the body, on account of worldly cares, and the gross ideas consequent thereupon, still they do so in the other life, where worldly and bodily things are removed...
Unless this truth is insinuated, man does not care for Heaven...
He who is in merely external pleasure takes care of his skin (that is, takes too much care of himself).
Some who in the life of the body have imbued the idea that man ought not to care for the things of the internal man...
He does not care whether (the poor whom he assists) are good or evil... AC 5028:end.
Instrumental things are not a subject of care. Signified, Explained.
If essential and not instrumental things are a subject of care to them, they will have instrumental things in abundance. Signified, Explained.
The Lord has such care for man, and that constantly...
It has sometimes happened that I thought much about worldly things, and about such things as are a subject of care to many... I then observed that I had relapsed into the Sensual...
When a man is in worldly cares... he is in sensuous life...
They who are in truth and not yet in good adore external things, and do not care for internal things...
Under Bless, see this reference. HH 401.
They do not care for the Lord. Signified.
They said that this is a sign that bodily and earthly things are more a subject of care (to the Spirits of our Earth) than heavenly things.
(The inhabitants of Jupiter) care little for worldly things... Their greatest care is the education of little children.
The scientifics which belong to human learning they do not care for.
Spiritual good given without any care of ours. Signified.
The Lord has not only a universal care...
Curing he shall cure () = restoration, namely, by interpretation. Explained.
The cares of the world and of the body (extinguish the light of Heaven).
Societies whose function it is to have the care of little children.
When he is such, he cares little for the things of Heaven...

There are many who have no internal acknowledgement of truth, and yet have the faith of charity, being those who in life have looked to the Lord, and from religion have avoided evils; but have been withheld by cares in the world and by business from thinking about truths.
According to their care...
According to the presence of their minds not distracted by cares...
For the sake of the care of infants...

On those who indulge too much in domestic cares. I saw a habitation rather deep down... there was a large room with utensils... through the court there went out a woman, small in stature, who was ugly... They who in the life of the body have been excessively devoted to domestic cares have such habitations, and are in their cares. Most of them are from the lower orders, like old women, who although such cares are no business of theirs, still assume them, like Martha, caring not for those things which are better, as the things of faith.
(On a state of freedom from bodily and worldly cares.)
(The Samaritan's saying) that they were to take care of him = that those who are instructed can heal him better than he could, being as yet in ignorance. AE 444:end.
